messages:
alex.m: Quick heads-up — during nightly dep scan we flagged two exploitable issues: CVE-2022-40045 in grpc/go (stream handling) and CVE-2023-31415 in github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go (signature parsing). Can we do a rapid triage and a minimal backport plan?

sara.t: Ack. I pulled the CVE entries. grpc fix landed in v1.55.0 with behavior change around stream flow control. jwt lib has a security patch in forked maintained repo at v3.3.1 that only changes parsing.

benji: Do we have any services still on older grpc modules? I know runtime pools and dedicated-gateway are pinned to older semver in a couple of repos.

caroline: runtime-service and auth-proxy are on go.mod: `google.golang.org/grpc v1.53.0` and `github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go v3.2.0` respectively.

alex.m: Thanks. Priority: auth-proxy (jwt) is high — public-facing token path. runtime-service (grpc) is medium but impacts internal streaming. Proposal: 1) immediate patch to auth-proxy bump to jwt fork v3.3.1 + run integration tests; 2) grpc bump to v1.55.0 staged canary 10% traffic, test streaming e2e.

benji: +1. For grpc, watch out for small API surface change around `MaxConcurrentStreams` defaults. We should add compatibility wrapper.

caroline: Suggest creating a tiny shim in runtime-service to preserve previous behavior if we detect old client headers. Example snippet: ```go
// compat_shim.go
func setStreamDefaults(s *grpc.Server) {
  // force the older default to avoid sudden throttling
  s.MaxConcurrentStreams = 1024
}
```

sec-bot: Security scan note: when bumping jwt, ensure `go mod tidy` and run `go vet` + `gosec` to catch any regressions. Recorded CVE IDs: CVE-2022-40045, CVE-2023-31415.

alex.m: Good. Can we allocate an engineer for quick backports? I'd like a short rollout checklist: patch branch, CI green, deploy to staging, run smoke + token fuzz test, canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 hours, monitor errors and p99 latency, rollback if error rate > 1% or auth failures spike.

sara.t: I'll take auth-proxy patch. Plan: branch `fix/jwt-cve-2023-31415`, bump `github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go` -> `github.com/form3tech-oss/jwt-go v3.3.1`, run unit/integration, post a PR with test evidence. Expected < 2h dev + CI.

benji: I'll handle runtime-service grpc shim + bump. Branch `fix/grpc-cve-2022-40045`. I'll add feature flag `grpc_compat_mode` so we can flip without full rollout.

caroline: Do we need any KMS or RBAC changes because of these bumps? jwt parsing changes shouldn't affect KMS. But auditors asked for audit-log markers for all security patches — we should add an AP audit event for deploys referencing the CVE.

alex.m: Yes — include audit log metadata on deploy: `security.fix_ids=["CVE-2022-40045","CVE-2023-31415"]`, `reviewer=sec-team`, `backport=true` fields. sec-bot can pick that up.

sec-bot: Noted. When PR merges, please add the deployment annotation via CLI: `redwoodctl deploy --annotate "security.fix_ids=CVE-2023-31415,CVE-2022-40045"`. I will ingest and attach to audit stream.

benji: One more: runtime-service uses a shared KV cache that is encrypted with KMS key `projects/redwood/keys/serving`. No key changes needed, but we'll include a quick smoke that verifies decrypt/attach during canary.

alex.m: Good call. Test plan summary in PR descriptions: unit + integration, canary verification (auth, stream), KMS decrypt smoke, and post-deploy verification script `scripts/sec-verif.sh` that checks logs for errors and validates JWTs.

caroline: Also ensure dependency tracking: update our internal SBOM entries and the dep-management spreadsheet so sales/compliance can see the change. I'll file a short one-pager to Legal.

benji: Timeline estimate: patches in next 4 hours, canary start in 6-8 hours if CI green.

alex.m: If CI fails for grpc due to behavior delta, fallback is to pin current grpc and publish an emergency advisory with mitigations (eg tighten client stream settings) while we prepare backport.

caroline: Create an incident-channel if anything goes sideways: #incidents/sec-dep-hotfix. I'll monitor.

sec-bot: Final automated action: creating issue in sec-triage board -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4821.

alex.m: Great work team — post PR links here when ready and remember to include `CHANGELOG.md` lines under Security. :thumbsup:
